# GitHub Workflows and Configurations

`velnor-gen` from [tailrocks/velnor-new](https://github.com/tailrocks/velnor-new) writes `rust-ci.yml` (from `.velnor/rust-ci.toml`, including the Alint and Jactionlint jobs from its `[[lint]]` entries and the Cargo Deny and Cargo Machete steps of its `policy` job) and every workflow declared in `.velnor/workflows.toml` (today `qualification.yml` and `tag-ruleset-drift.yml`), and `release.yml` from `.velnor/release.toml` (the `tools-v` release of `velnor-ci` and `velnor-gen`). Each starts with the `# Generated by velnor-gen.` header. Do not hand-edit them: change their inputs and run `velnor-gen generate`, and `velnor-gen check` exits 1 on drift.

The other files under `.github/` are repository-owned: `workflows/ci.yml` is hand-written (the `workflow_dispatch` contract inputs and the helper-gates check), and so are the configuration files `dco.yml` and `jactionlint.yaml`.

## What the helper-gate check guards

`scripts/check-helper-gates.sh` is a lint, so it is a fast early warning and not the guard. It lexes each changed file whole, carrying comment, string and raw-string state across lines so that text inside a string or a comment is not counted, and then judges the added lines. It cannot parse Rust, so it rejects only what it can recognise without doubt and accepts the rest. A file moved into the gate crates unchanged (a git rename) adds nothing. It rejects an unmarked released gate written as a literal `(0, 1, N)` tuple or as a bare `0.1.N` token in code, a marker that does not name the gate's release, a change of `HELPER_MINIMUM` (one line, or the `(0, 1, N);` line directly under a split `HELPER_MINIMUM ... =` line; a bare `(0, 1, N);` elsewhere is not counted as a change of it) without the marker of a released helper, and, in `crates/velnor-gen/src/key_gates/`, a tuple that starts with the literals `0, 1,` and closes on the same line with anything but one integer literal. It also rejects the phrases "first released in" and "not tagged yet" in `generator/CONFIG.md` and `docs/rust-ci.md`, and in an added line in the gate crates only when the line starts with a comment (`//`, `/*` or `*`); a trailing comment after code is not matched. A gate written any other way (`(0, 1 as u64, 110)`, `(0, 1, 100 + 10)` in a constant, a tuple split over lines) passes the lint.

The guard against new behaviour at a released pin is byte-identical rendering. A gate that changes output at 0.1.110 or 0.1.111 changes the output that `velnor-gen check` compares with the committed workflows, and the `golden` and `drift` tests compare with every sample and with this repository's own workflows, whatever form the gate tuple takes.

The render guard has a limit: it catches a gate only when some sample repository (the golden samples) or this repository's own workflows render the configuration the gate guards. A gate that changes output only for a configuration that no sample and no committed workflow renders turns nothing red, so a new gated behaviour needs a sample (or a test) that renders it.

## Workflow Issues and Enhancements

When issues, bugs, limitations, or enhancements are observed in a generated workflow:

1. **Do NOT patch generated outputs or create repo-specific workarounds**: no local patches, overrides, or shims in a generated file.
2. **Fix the generator**: change `velnor-gen` under `generator/` (or the declaration in `.velnor/`), then regenerate with `velnor-gen generate`.
3. **Verify** the change against the generator's golden samples (`generator/TESTING.md`) before it merges.

## Root Repository Rules

- If a root `AGENTS.md` is present in this repository, all of its rules, invariants, and guidelines apply here as well.
- In case of conflict, stricter safety, correctness, and verification standards take precedence.
